html:
The Comoros declared independence from France on 6 July 1975, after a referendum in which three islands voted to leave, but Mayotte voted to stay French.

France had bought Mayotte in 1841 and made the other islands protectorates in the 1880s, ruling them as part of Madagascar until 1946. In the referendum of December 1974 the islands overall voted for independence, but Mayotte, where many had long distrusted the other islands, voted against. France counted the islands one by one and kept Mayotte.

Ahmed Abdallah declared independence unilaterally, and was overthrown within a month with help from the mercenary Bob Denard. The Comoros still claims Mayotte, which became a French department in 2011 and draws many migrants from the other islands.
sum: The Comoros declared independence from France on 6 July 1975, after a referendum in which three islands voted to leave, but Mayotte voted to stay French.
